\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{முக்கியத்துவம்} (mukkiyattuvam)}{முக்கியத்துவம் (mukkiyattuvam)}]{\ta{முக்கியத்துவம்} (mukkiyattuvam) — importance}

\label{lesson:TA-C354-mukkiyattuvam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for an evil, then the Tamil for a benefit.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{முக்கியத்துவம்}}
\textbf{\ta{முக்கியத்துவம்}} — \emph{mukkiyattuvam} — \textquotedblleft{}importance\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{கல்விக்கு} \ta{அதிக} \ta{முக்கியத்துவம்} \ta{கொடுக்க} \ta{வேண்டும்}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kalvikku atika mukkiyattuvam koṭukka vēṇṭum.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We must give more importance to education.
\end{quote}

X-\ta{க்கு} \ta{முக்கியத்துவம்} \ta{கொடு}, to give importance to X. The adjective is \ta{முக்கியமான}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{முக்கியத்துவம்}} (\emph{mukkiyattuvam}) is built on Sanskrit \emph{mukhya}, \textquotedblleft{}chief, principal\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 10174), the source of \ta{முக்கியமான}, with the Sanskrit abstract suffix \emph{-tva}, \textquotedblleft{}-ness\textquotedblright{}, which Tamil writes -\ta{த்துவம்}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mukkiyattuvam}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mukkiyattuvam}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kalvikku atika mukkiyattuvam koṭukka vēṇṭum.} — We must give more importance to education.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for an evil, then the Tamil for a benefit, then say \emph{mukkiyattuvam} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{முக்கியத்துவம்} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Importance\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{முன்னுரிமை} (muṉṉurimai)}{முன்னுரிமை (muṉṉurimai)}]{\ta{முன்னுரிமை} (muṉṉurimai) — a priority}

\label{lesson:TA-C354-munnurimai}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for a benefit, then the Tamil for importance.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{முன்னுரிமை}}
\textbf{\ta{முன்னுரிமை}} — \emph{muṉṉurimai} — \textquotedblleft{}a priority\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{நோயாளிகளுக்கு} \ta{முன்னுரிமை} \ta{கொடுக்கப்படும்}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{nōyāḷikaḷukku muṉṉurimai koṭukkappaṭum.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Patients will be given priority.
\end{quote}

X-\ta{க்கு} \ta{முன்னுரிமை} \ta{கொடு}, to give X priority.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{முன்னுரிமை}} (\emph{muṉṉurimai}) is native: \emph{muṉ}, \textquotedblleft{}in front, before\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 5020), and \emph{urimai}, \textquotedblleft{}a right, a claim\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 654): the right to go first.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{muṉṉurimai}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nōyāḷikaḷukku muṉṉurimai koṭukkappaṭum.} — Patients will be given priority.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for a benefit, then the Tamil for importance, then say \emph{muṉṉurimai} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{அம்சம்} (amcam)}{அம்சம் (amcam)}]{\ta{அம்சம்} (amcam) — an aspect; a feature}

\label{lesson:TA-C354-amcam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for importance, then the Tamil for a priority.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{அம்சம்}}
\textbf{\ta{அம்சம்}} — \emph{amcam} — \textquotedblleft{}an aspect; a feature\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{இந்தத்} \ta{திட்டத்தின்} \ta{முக்கியமான} \ta{அம்சம்} \ta{இதுதான்}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{intat tiṭṭattiṉ mukkiyamāṉa amcam itutāṉ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
This is the main feature of the plan.
\end{quote}

Plural: \ta{அம்சங்கள்}, \emph{amcaṅkaḷ}.

Plural \ta{அம்சங்கள்}: \ta{பல} \ta{அம்சங்கள்}, many aspects.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{அம்சம்}} (\emph{amcam}) is borrowed from Sanskrit \emph{aṃśa}, \textquotedblleft{}share, part\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 2): one part of a whole, so one aspect of it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{amcam}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{intat tiṭṭattiṉ mukkiyamāṉa amcam itutāṉ.} — This is the main feature of the plan.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for importance, then the Tamil for a priority, then say \emph{amcam} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{தேவை} (tēvai)}{தேவை (tēvai)}]{\ta{தேவை} (tēvai) — a need; a requirement}

\label{lesson:TA-C354-tevai}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for a priority, then the Tamil for an aspect.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{தேவை}}
\textbf{\ta{தேவை}} — \emph{tēvai} — \textquotedblleft{}a need; a requirement\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{மக்களின்} \ta{தேவைகளை} \ta{அரசு} \ta{கவனிக்க} \ta{வேண்டும்}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{makkaḷiṉ tēvaikaḷai aracu kavaṉikka vēṇṭum.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The government must attend to the needs of the people.
\end{quote}

Plural: \ta{தேவைகள்}, \emph{tēvaikaḷ}.

\ta{எனக்கு} \ta{ஒரு} \ta{புத்தகம்} \ta{தேவை}, I need a book: the person in the dative. \ta{தேவையில்லை}, there is no need.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{தேவை}} (\emph{tēvai}) is native Dravidian: DEDR 3469 lists Tamil \emph{tēvai}, \textquotedblleft{}affairs; compelling need, necessity\textquotedblright{}, with Malayalam \emph{tēva}, \textquotedblleft{}need\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tēvai}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{makkaḷiṉ tēvaikaḷai aracu kavaṉikka vēṇṭum.} — The government must attend to the needs of the people.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for a priority, then the Tamil for an aspect, then say \emph{tēvai} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ta{வலியுறுத்து} (valiyuṟuttu)}{வலியுறுத்து (valiyuṟuttu)}]{\ta{வலியுறுத்து} (valiyuṟuttu) — to stress; to insist on}

\label{lesson:TA-C354-valiyuruttu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for an aspect, then the Tamil for a need.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{வலியுறுத்து}}
\textbf{\ta{வலியுறுத்து}} — \emph{valiyuṟuttu} — \textquotedblleft{}to stress; to insist on\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ta{மருத்துவர்} \ta{ஓய்வின்} \ta{முக்கியத்துவத்தை} \ta{வலியுறுத்தினார்}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{maruttuvar ōyviṉ mukkiyattuvattai valiyuṟuttiṉār.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The doctor stressed the importance of rest.
\end{quote}

Past (I …): \ta{வலியுறுத்தினேன்}, \emph{valiyuṟuttiṉēṉ}.

What is stressed takes -\ta{ஐ}: X-\ta{ஐ} \ta{வலியுறுத்து}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ta{வலியுறுத்து}} (\emph{valiyuṟuttu}) is native: \emph{vali}, \textquotedblleft{}strength, force\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 5276), and \emph{uṟuttu}, \textquotedblleft{}to impress strongly upon the mind\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 712): to press a point with force.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[(dialogue)]{Looking back: reasons and arguments}

\label{lesson:TA-R354-review-347-354}



\begin{quote}
Say the Tamil for evidence and to prove.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item evidence, to prove, logic, a basis, an explanation
  \item to oppose, to object, to argue, a consensus, some people
  \item to think deeply, to guess, to assume, a hypothesis, many people
  \item a point of view, a stand, an attitude, an angle, to express
  \item to mention, to indicate, to expound, that is to say, an example
  \item to cause, an impact, a factor, to lead to, to affect
  \item an advantage, a drawback, goodness, an evil, a benefit
  \item importance, a priority, an aspect, a need, to stress
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Evidence? (\textbf{\ta{ஆதாரம்}}, \emph{ātāram}.) To prove? (\textbf{\ta{நிரூபி}}, \emph{nirūpi}.) Logic? (\textbf{\ta{தர்க்கம்}}, \emph{tarkkam}.) A basis? (\textbf{\ta{அடிப்படை}}, \emph{aṭippaṭai}.) An explanation? (\textbf{\ta{விளக்கம்}}, \emph{viḷakkam}.) To oppose? (\textbf{\ta{எதிர்}}, \emph{etir}.) To object? (\textbf{\ta{ஆட்சேபி}}, \emph{āṭcēpi}.) To argue? (\textbf{\ta{வாதிடு}}, \emph{vātiṭu}.) A consensus? (\textbf{\ta{உடன்பாடு}}, \emph{uṭaṉpāṭu}.) Some people? (\textbf{\ta{சிலர்}}, \emph{cilar}.) To think deeply? (\textbf{\ta{சிந்தி}}, \emph{cinti}.) To guess? (\textbf{\ta{ஊகி}}, \emph{ūki}.) To assume? (\textbf{\ta{அனுமானி}}, \emph{aṉumāṉi}.) A hypothesis? (\textbf{\ta{கருதுகோள்}}, \emph{karutukōḷ}.) Many people? (\textbf{\ta{பலர்}}, \emph{palar}.) A point of view? (\textbf{\ta{கண்ணோட்டம்}}, \emph{kaṇṇōṭṭam}.) A stand? (\textbf{\ta{நிலைப்பாடு}}, \emph{nilaippāṭu}.) An attitude? (\textbf{\ta{மனப்பான்மை}}, \emph{maṉappāṉmai}.) An angle? (\textbf{\ta{கோணம்}}, \emph{kōṇam}.) To express? (\textbf{\ta{வெளிப்படுத்து}}, \emph{veḷippaṭuttu}.) To mention? (\textbf{\ta{குறிப்பிடு}}, \emph{kuṟippiṭu}.) To indicate? (\textbf{\ta{சுட்டிக்காட்டு}}, \emph{cuṭṭikkāṭṭu}.) To expound? (\textbf{\ta{எடுத்துரை}}, \emph{eṭutturai}.) That is to say? (\textbf{\ta{அதாவது}}, \emph{atāvatu}.) An example? (\textbf{\ta{எடுத்துக்காட்டு}}, \emph{eṭuttukkāṭṭu}.) To cause? (\textbf{\ta{ஏற்படுத்து}}, \emph{ēṟpaṭuttu}.) An impact? (\textbf{\ta{தாக்கம்}}, \emph{tākkam}.) A factor? (\textbf{\ta{காரணி}}, \emph{kāraṇi}.) To lead to? (\textbf{\ta{வழிவகு}}, \emph{vaḻivaku}.) To affect? (\textbf{\ta{பாதி}}, \emph{pāti}.) An advantage? (\textbf{\ta{சாதகம்}}, \emph{cātakam}.) A drawback? (\textbf{\ta{பாதகம்}}, \emph{pātakam}.) Goodness? (\textbf{\ta{நன்மை}}, \emph{naṉmai}.) An evil? (\textbf{\ta{தீமை}}, \emph{tīmai}.) A benefit? (\textbf{\ta{பலன்}}, \emph{palaṉ}.) Importance? (\textbf{\ta{முக்கியத்துவம்}}, \emph{mukkiyattuvam}.) A priority? (\textbf{\ta{முன்னுரிமை}}, \emph{muṉṉurimai}.) An aspect? (\textbf{\ta{அம்சம்}}, \emph{amcam}.) A need? (\textbf{\ta{தேவை}}, \emph{tēvai}.) To stress? (\textbf{\ta{வலியுறுத்து}}, \emph{valiyuṟuttu}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
